node.label: Hannah Arendt
node.date_label: The Origins of Totalitarianism (1951) · The Human Condition (1958) · Eichmann in Jerusalem (1963) · Günter Gaus interview: politics and factual truth (1964)
node.description: Examines political action, public speech and the responsibility to preserve factual truth. In the selected 1964 Gaus interview she treats speaking and acting as ventures into relations with other people whose consequences cannot be predicted completely. Her defense of historical factual truth resists treating facts as mere opinion or allowing official rewriting to erase inconvenient persons and events. Her response to the Eichmann controversy is testimony from a participant in that controversy, not an independent verdict on every disputed judgment in the book. The profile distinguishes the primary interview selection from unread monographs and from the institutional bibliography that establishes their dates.
